candidates.name: Haditha–Baniyas Oil Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Iraq Ministry of Oil (feasibility study); studied in parallel by a consortium of Capital TI (US), Chevron (US) and UCC Holding (Qatar) alongside Basra Oil Company
candidates.from: Haditha, Anbar, Iraq (terminus of the Basra–Haditha trunk pipeline, P0544)

evidence.note: MEES: Iraq's oil ministry announced (25 Jan 2026) it is conducting feasibility studies for a new pipeline linking Haditha to Syria's Baniyas terminal, building on the approved Basra-Haditha pipeline as the launch point.

Iraq Business News: Oil Minister Hayan Abdul-Ghani chaired a meeting (28 Jan 2026) on the implementation plan for the Haditha-Baniyas crude pipeline, instructing acceleration of remaining technical/logistical studies.
The National: construction started on the Basra-Haditha trunk (1 May 2026); Oil Ministry plans branches from Haditha toward Jordan (Aqaba) and toward Baniyas (Syria) for export.

Iraqi News Agency (INA): Iraq considers new oil pipeline to Syrian port of Baniyas (200 OK, contains 'Baniyas'; page blocked automated fetch, content not independently re-read beyond the verifier's substring check).

candidates.why_maybe_new: Every existing GEM row for a Kirkuk-Baniyas corridor (P5278, P7913, P5279, P0546, P5277) has Kirkuk as the Iraqi origin, and a separate Dec-2025 press cluster (Syrian-Iraqi committees, worldpipelines.com) describes a straight revival of that same Kirkuk->Baniyas route (not treated as a discovery here since it matches those PIDs). This Haditha-Baniyas project is described as a distinct branch off the NEW Basra-Haditha trunk (P0544, under construction) originating at Haditha rather than Kirkuk -- no existing PID has Haditha as an endpoint toward Baniyas (the only Haditha-outbound proposed branch on the roster is P5240, Haditha->Aqaba). Flagging as a possible discovery, but the consolidator should watch for these two Baniyas-bound efforts (Kirkuk-origin revival vs. Haditha-origin new branch) converging into a single project once Iraq picks a final route.

candidates.name: Basra–Fishkhabur–Ceyhan Oil Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Consortium: Capital TI (US), Chevron (US), UCC Holding (Qatar), and an Iraqi state oil company (Basra Oil Company), per Iraqi cabinet-approved preliminary agreement
candidates.from: Basra, Iraq (via the Basra–Haditha trunk, P0544)
candidates.to: Fish Khabur (Iraq-Turkey border) connecting to Ceyhan terminal, Turkey

evidence.note: Iraqi News: Oil Minister Basim Khudair said a consortium of TI Capital, Chevron and Qatar's UCC will build a pipeline system from Basra to Fish Khabur, connecting to Ceyhan, with a branch from Haditha to Baniyas.

Iraqi News: cabinet approved (5 Jul 2026) an agreement between Basra Oil Company and the Capital TI/Chevron/UCC consortium to conduct feasibility studies comparing Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan vs. Basra-Haditha-Baniyas routes; ~2 million bbl/d capacity cited by officials, no signed construction contract yet.

Enerdata: summarizes the Basra-Haditha trunk (2.25 mb/d) and confirms Oil Ministry intent to add branches from Haditha toward Jordan and toward Baniyas, distinct from the resumed (separate, existing) Kirkuk-Ceyhan flow.

candidates.why_maybe_new: Closest existing PIDs by geography are P0547 (Kirkuk-Ceyhan, operating) and P1854 (Kirkuk-Ceyhan / Beji-Fishkhabur Replacement aka New Iraq-Turkiye Crude Oil Pipeline, cancelled) -- both originate at Kirkuk or Beji. This newly-announced (Jul 2026) consortium project would build a new connector from the Basra-Haditha trunk (P0544) north to Fish Khabur/Ceyhan, i.e. a different southern origin (Basra/Haditha, not Kirkuk/Beji) even if it ultimately ties into the same Turkish Ceyhan corridor. Still pre-FID (cabinet-approved feasibility study only, no route/length/diameter/cost confirmed) -- flag for the consolidator to decide whether this supersedes/reactivates P1854 or is a genuinely separate row; if judged the same project as P1854 under a new sponsor, it may belong as a status/aka update to P1854 rather than a new row.
